_note: Research groups shown on groups.html (the quantum research groups at the five universities). Summaries are written by Danish Quantum Academy; quotes are short excerpts from the group's own page. Members, publications and projects come from data/groups/<key>.txt; news, events and positions from data/groups/feeds.json (refreshed weekly by scripts/fetch_group_feeds.py).

groups.name: Quantum Physics and Information Technology (QPIT)
groups.quote: to understand, to engineer, and to control complex quantum systems of light and matter
groups.summary: A DTU Physics section that builds quantum systems of light and matter and uses them for computing, communication and sensing. Main lines are optical quantum computing with squeezed light and cluster states, continuous-variable quantum key distribution, quantum sensing with NV centres in diamond, and quantum optomechanics. The section is part of the bigQ centre (Center for Macroscopic Quantum States), the Copenhagen Center for Biomedical Quantum Sensing (CBQS) and Biomag.
themes: Optical quantum computing with squeezed light
centres: Copenhagen Center for Biomedical Quantum Sensing

groups.name: NanoPhoton – Center for Nanophotonics
groups.unit: Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering
groups.summary: A DTU centre of excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation that designs and fabricates dielectric nanocavities which squeeze light far below the wavelength. The work spans nanolasers and cavity quantum electrodynamics, quantum dots and other quantum emitters in semiconductors and 2D materials, topology optimisation of photonic structures, and nano-opto-electro-mechanical devices for photonic information processing and quantum light sources.
themes: Quantum emitters in semiconductors and 2D materials
centres: Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence

groups.name: Quantum Light Sources
groups.unit: Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering
groups.summary: A DTU Electro group that designs, models and fabricates sources of single and entangled photons for quantum technology. It combines quantum-mechanical theory of single-photon emitters with semiconductor quantum dots in micropillars and nanoposts, telecom-band quantum dots, 2D-material quantum emitters and superconducting single-photon detectors, and integrates emitters with silicon nitride photonics for remote quantum computing.

groups.name: Quantum Networks
groups.unit: Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering
groups.summary: A small DTU Electro group working on quantum photonic devices for quantum networks. It grows and studies semiconductor nanowire quantum dots and multi-quantum-dot systems as sources of single photons and as location qubits, aiming at multi-qubit quantum photonic devices.

groups.name: Quantum Communication Systems
groups.unit: Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering
groups.summary: A DTU Electro group that builds quantum communication systems on optical fibre and photonic chips. Work covers quantum key distribution multiplexed over few-mode fibre, co-existence of quantum and classical signals in the same network, and on-chip quantum random number generators.
themes: Quantum key distribution over multi-mode fibre
Co-existence of quantum and classical communication

groups.name: Magnetic Resonance by Optics
groups.summary: A DTU Health Tech group that uses nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond as quantum sensors in biology. It traps fluorescent nanodiamonds with laser light inside living cells and reads out their spin to sense free radicals, magnetic fields and the mechanics of cells, for example in models of cardiac fibrosis, atherosclerosis and cancer.

groups.name: Quantum Information Science & Technology (NQCP)
groups.summary: The Niels Bohr Institute unit behind the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP), with its own website at nqcp.ku.dk. Its members work across the stack of a future quantum computer: superconducting and hybrid superconductor–semiconductor qubits, spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots, photonic qubits from colour centres in silicon, quantum algorithms for chemistry and open quantum systems, and strontium atomic clocks.
themes: Quantum algorithms for chemistry and open systems
centres: Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme

groups.name: QMATH – Centre for the Mathematics of Quantum Theory
teacher_units: Centre for the Mathematics of Quantum Theory
groups.quote: contribute to our mathematical understanding of quantum physics
groups.summary: A VILLUM centre of excellence at the Department of Mathematical Sciences, working where mathematics, physics and computer science meet. It studies the mathematics behind quantum matter and quantum information: many-body quantum systems and their ground states, quantum information theory and entropies, quantum algorithms, simulation and learning, nonlocal games and quantum walks. VILLUM renewed the support with an Investor grant for 2026–2031.
themes: Mathematical physics of many-body quantum systems

groups.name: Quantum Optics and Photonics
groups.summary: A Niels Bohr Institute section for experimental and theoretical quantum optics. Its groups build deterministic single-photon sources with quantum dots in photonic chips, entangle atomic ensembles with light and mechanical oscillators for quantum sensing beyond the standard quantum limit, develop membrane optomechanics, and work on Rydberg-atom quantum optics and quantum networks. The section also does research on quantum technology education and the quantum job market.
themes: Atomic ensembles and hybrid quantum networks

groups.name: Condensed Matter Physics (incl. Center for Quantum Devices)
groups.summary: A Niels Bohr Institute section whose quantum work centres on the Center for Quantum Devices and condensed matter theory: hybrid semiconductor–superconductor qubits and Josephson junction arrays, spin qubits in quantum dots, Majorana and Andreev bound states, and unconventional superconductivity. The section also has groups in neutron and X-ray scattering and soft matter.
themes: Semiconductor quantum dots and spin qubits
centres: Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme

groups.name: Center for Complex Quantum Systems (CCQ)
groups.quote: advance our understanding of collective quantum phenomena in large collections of particles
groups.summary: A Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence at Aarhus University, started in September 2020. It studies collective quantum behaviour in many atoms, ions and photons and builds hybrid systems where these meet: ion Coulomb crystals and ion traps (Drewsen), Bose–Einstein condensates and impurities (Arlt) and theory of polarons and many-body physics (Bruun). Former founding groups of Klaus Mølmer (now KU) and Thomas Pohl (now TU Wien) remain partners.
centres: Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence

groups.name: Chen group – VILLUM Center for Hybrid Quantum Materials and Devices (HQMD)
groups.unit: Department of Physics and Astronomy and iNANO
teacher_units: Villum Center for Hybrid Quantum Materials and Devices
groups.summary: Yong P. Chen's group at AU runs the VILLUM Center for Hybrid Quantum Materials and Devices. It combines different quantum electronic and photonic systems, such as 2D materials, topological materials and their heterostructures, to discover new quantum matter and to build devices and measurement methods for future quantum computing, communication and sensing.

groups.name: Quantum Materials Group
groups.quote: lay the foundations for next generation quantum technologies
groups.summary: An experimental condensed matter group at the ASTRID2 synchrotron in Aarhus led by Jill Miwa. It grows atomically thin quantum materials and maps their electronic and structural properties with scanning tunnelling microscopy and nanoARPES, including in working devices. Topics include transition metal dichalcogenides, van der Waals heterostructures and phosphorus delta-layers in silicon, a platform for silicon spin qubits (the DeltaQT project with the Niels Bohr Institute).
themes: Delta-layers in silicon for spin qubits

groups.name: Ultrafast Dynamics of Quantum Materials
groups.quote: to explore and control the properties of materials
groups.summary: An AU physics group that uses ultrashort laser pulses to follow and steer quantum materials on their natural time scales. It studies atomic, spin and electron dynamics, light-induced phase transitions, orbital order and coherent phonons, and nonlinear optics in materials such as high-temperature superconductors.

groups.name: Department of Physics and Astronomy – other quantum researchers
groups.summary: Quantum researchers at AU's Department of Physics and Astronomy who are not part of CCQ, HQMD, the Quantum Materials Group or the ultrafast group. They are listed under their department, not as a group. Topics include quantum computing theory and quantum algorithms for chemistry, quantum many-body physics with transmon qubits, Rydberg atoms, cavity optomechanics, spin ensembles, open quantum systems and national quantum strategies.

groups.name: Department of Chemistry – quantum researchers
groups.summary: Quantum chemists at AU's Department of Chemistry working on quantum computing for chemistry, listed under their department. They develop vibrational coupled cluster methods and fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for molecular vibrational wave functions, together with the Department of Physics and Astronomy.

groups.name: Department of Computer Science – quantum and post-quantum researchers
groups.summary: Researchers at AU's Department of Computer Science working on quantum and post-quantum topics, listed under their department. They include cryptographers designing post-quantum protocols and studying isogenies, researchers on simulation and minimal size of quantum circuits, and quantum information theory.

groups.name: Department of Mathematics – quantum researchers
groups.summary: Mathematical physics of quantum systems at AU's Department of Mathematics, listed under the department.

groups.name: Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA)
groups.summary: A Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence at SDU's Mads Clausen Institute. It studies how light couples to matter at the nanoscale through polaritons: quantum and nonlocal plasmonics in metals, polaritons in graphene and other 2D materials, excitons, free-electron–light interaction and cathodoluminescence. The work is mostly theory, with experiments in electron-beam spectroscopy and nanophotonics.
centres: Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence

groups.name: QM – Centre for Quantum Mathematics
groups.unit: Department of Mathematics and Computer Science
groups.quote: to advance research and education in quantum mathematics
groups.summary: An SDU centre founded in 2019 for the mathematics underlying quantum theory and quantum technologies. Research covers quantum topology and topological quantum field theory, geometric quantisation, quantum field theory and categorical symmetries of quantum matter. Its quantum computing initiative works on photonic quantum computing (TopQC2X), Gaussian boson sampling and applications in pharma, finance and climate together with the spin-out Qpurpose, and it runs SDU's MSc programme in quantum computing.
themes: Quantum field theory and symmetries of quantum matter
Quantum algorithms for pharma, finance and climate

groups.name: SDU Nano Optics
groups.summary: An SDU group in plasmonics and metasurfaces. Its quantum work concerns quantum metasurfaces that generate and shape single photons, chip-integrated single-photon sources from colour centres in nanodiamonds, and room-temperature indistinguishable single photons; it also develops electrically tunable and nonlocal metasurfaces for classical optics.

groups.name: Classique – Center for Classical Communication in the Quantum Era
teacher_units: Classique – Center for Classical Communication in the Quantum Era
Classical and Quantum Information and Connectivity
groups.quote: revolutionize communication systems for the quantum age
groups.summary: A Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence at Aalborg University (2025–2031). It asks how classical communication networks must change to serve both ordinary data and quantum information, which is fragile and time-limited. Researchers from communication engineering, physics, mathematics and computer science work on hybrid classical–quantum and satellite networks, physics-based models of quantum components, data compression and coding, and verification of quantum protocols.
centres: Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence

groups.name: Quantum Systems Analysis and Synthesis
groups.quote: develops methods and tools to empower developers in the field of quantum computing
groups.summary: A group in AAU's Department of Computer Science that brings formal methods to the quantum software stack. It works on verification and validation of quantum circuits and communication protocols (for example with the UPPAAL model checker), equivalence checking with tensor decision diagrams and machine learning, and design automation for quantum software. It leads ODAQS, a national project with Kvantify on a performant quantum software stack for drug discovery.
themes: Model checking of quantum communication protocols
Design automation for the quantum software stack
centres: Classique – Center for Classical Communication in the Quantum Era
